title: Derived base change of a relatively flat closed kernel on a product of algebraic spaces
statement:
Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme] and algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the canonical module functors [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], and derived tensor pullback computed by K-flat resolutions [def-sfb-space-derived-pullback]. Let $S_0$ be a scheme, let $X_0,Y_0$ be algebraic spaces over $S_0$, and let $a:S\to S_0$ be any scheme morphism. Put $T_0=X_0\times_{S_0}Y_0$, $T=T_0\times_{S_0}S$, and let $q:T\to T_0$ be projection [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $i_0:W_0\hookrightarrow T_0$ be a closed immersion, meaning representable by closed immersions on scheme tests [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume $Y_0\to S_0$ and $W_0\to T_0\to X_0$ are flat, meaning flat on compatible etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Form $W=W_0\times_{T_0}T$, with projection $r:W\to W_0$ and closed immersion $i:W\hookrightarrow T$. There is a canonical isomorphism in the derived category
$$Lq^*((i_{0,*}\mathcal O_{W_0})[0])\simeq(i_*\mathcal O_W)[0]\quad\text{in }D(\mathcal O_T).$$
It is the derived base-change comparison $Lq^*Ri_{0,*}\mathcal O_{W_0}\to Ri_*Lr^*\mathcal O_{W_0}$ under the identifications $Lr^*\mathcal O_{W_0}=\mathcal O_W$ and derived closed pushforward of the structure sheaf with its degree-zero ordinary pushforward. No flatness of $a$, $X_0\to S_0$ or $i_0$, and no Noetherian or finiteness assumptions, are imposed.

source.place: Tag 0CTQ, lemma-case-of-tor-independence; Tag 08IR, lemma-compare-base-change, applied to a closed immersion and its structure sheaf.

proof.text: Put $X=X_0\times_{S_0}S$ and $Y=Y_0\times_{S_0}S$. The fibre-product universal property identifies $X\times_SY$ with $T$: on every test scheme both have triples $(x_0,y_0,s)$ whose images in $S_0$ agree. The projection to $T_0$ is $q$ under this identification. The same universal property identifies its inverse image of $W_0$ with the stated $W$, with projections $r,i$.

source.place: Tag 0CTQ, lemma-case-of-tor-independence: its notation for the base-changed product.

proof.text: Apply the product Tor-independence lemma to the square with corners $Z_0=W_0$, $X_0$, $Y_0$, $B_0=S_0$, the map $W_0\to Y_0$ induced by $i_0$, and $B=S$. Take its ambient scheme to be $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. The square commutes because $i_0$ maps to the product. Its two flatness assumptions are exactly $Y_0/S_0$ and $W_0/X_0$, which are hypotheses here. By step 1 its conclusion says that $i_0$ and $q$ are Tor independent over $T_0$.

source.place: Tag 0CTQ, lemma-case-of-tor-independence, specialized to the displayed product.

proof.text: For every scheme test $U\to T$, the fibre-product equations give $W\times_TU\simeq W_0\times_{T_0}U$. The latter is a closed subscheme of $U$ by the representable closed-immersion hypothesis, so $i$ is closed. On an affine test of either $T_0$ or $T$, the closed source is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ by the affine characterization of closed immersions. Thus $i_0$ and $i$ are affine. The affine-locality lemma makes $i_0$ quasi-compact and separated, in particular quasi-separated, as required for derived base change.

source.place: Closed immersions on scheme tests; Tag 01QO, lemma-closed-immersion (affine quotient characterization); affine locality and qcqs permanence.

proof.text: The structure sheaf has the rank-one free local presentation, so is quasi-coherent. Closed pushforward gives quasi-coherent $i_{0,*}\mathcal O_{W_0}$ and $i_*\mathcal O_W$. Apply affine module higher-image vanishing to both maps of step 3 and these structure modules. Their canonical maps from degree-zero ordinary pushforward to derived pushforward are isomorphisms: positive cohomology is the vanishing $R^j i_*$, negative cohomology is zero for a degree-zero injective resolution, and degree zero is ordinary direct image. The comparison is therefore a quasi-isomorphism.

The complex $\mathcal O_{W_0}[0]$ is K-flat directly from the definition: tensoring any acyclic complex with it gives that same complex. It can therefore serve as its own K-flat resolution for $Lr^*$. Ordinary tensor pullback sends it to $\mathcal O_W[0]$: multiplication $b\otimes c\mapsto b\,r^\sharp(c)$ is inverse to $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. These are the canonical tensor-unit identifications, without flatness of $r$.

source.place: K-flat derived tensor pullback; ordinary tensor-unit calculation (Tags 06YV, 03D7).

proof.text: Apply Tor-independent derived base change with $f=i_0$, $g=q$, $f^\prime=i$, $g^\prime=r$, and $E=\mathcal O_{W_0}[0]$. Step 2 supplies Tor independence, step 3 supplies qcqs, and step 4 supplies quasi-coherence of $E$. This gives the canonical isomorphism $Lq^*Ri_{0,*}E\to Ri_*Lr^*E$. Substitute the canonical identifications of steps 4 and 5 to obtain the isomorphism claimed in the item. The morphism is exactly the adjunction-mate comparison specified by the cited theorem; only its source and target have been identified.
